question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit at Positive or Negative Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
question.worked_solution:
Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\sqrt{x}=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{ln}^{2}⁡x=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\sqrt{x}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[\sqrt{x}]^{′}}{{[{ln}^{2}⁡x]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})}{(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x}{4\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\sqrt{x}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

The resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\sqrt{x}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\sqrt{x}}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[\sqrt{x}]^{′}}{[4\operatorname{ln}⁡x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})}{(\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x}{8\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\sqrt{x} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
